{
  "per_column": [
    {
      "name": "asset_category",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.85,
      "source_groundedness": 0.9,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Categorizes CIs into meaningful asset types (hardware, cloud, travel), giving a strong grouping axis. Values are well-grounded in the ci/short_description text (e.g. Dell Latitude -> hardware_endpoint, AWS EC2 -> cloud_service)."
    },
    {
      "name": "ci_form_factor",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.7,
      "source_groundedness": 0.9,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Finer-grained form factor (laptop/desktop/server) is derivable from ci strings and adds a useful sub-grouping. Partially redundant with asset_category but still a distinct axis. Well grounded."
    },
    {
      "name": "travel_context",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.8,
      "source_groundedness": 0.85,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Directly relevant to the travel-expense query, separating travel vs non-travel items. Grounded in source text, though the dominance of 'not_travel' for hardware raises questions about whether these are truly travel expenses."
    },
    {
      "name": "asset_brand",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.75,
      "source_groundedness": 0.9,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Brand extraction (Dell, HP, AWS, Samsonite) offers a genuine axis for spend/vendor analysis and is directly extractable from ci strings."
    },
    {
      "name": "record_action_type",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.7,
      "source_groundedness": 0.8,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Categorizes lifecycle action (procurement/registration/provisioning) from short_description; a reasonable inference and useful for grouping. Some categories (allocation, maintenance_upgrade) rely on inference but appear warranted."
    },
    {
      "name": "creation_method",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.6,
      "source_groundedness": 0.95,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Manual vs automated is clearly cued by phrases like 'Automated creation'/'Automatically generated'. A binary flag but offers a legitimate comparison axis; well grounded."
    },
    {
      "name": "processing_lag_band",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.75,
      "source_groundedness": 0.85,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Bands the lag between opened_at and processed_date, a useful operational-efficiency axis. Derivable from date columns; 'not_processed' correctly handles nan dates."
    },
    {
      "name": "source_id_present",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.35,
      "source_groundedness": 0.95,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "A bare presence/absence flag on an existing column; low analytical leverage and largely trivial, though correctly grounded."
    },
    {
      "name": "department_group",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.4,
      "source_groundedness": 0.55,
      "hallucination_observed": true,
      "rationale": "Appears near-redundant with the existing 'department' column. More concerning, department is not present in the sampled source_text yet specific groups (Customer_Support, Sales) are asserted per row, so groundedness cannot be confirmed and values may be invented relative to shown evidence."
    },
    {
      "name": "is_miscellaneous_ci",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.3,
      "source_groundedness": 0.85,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Near-constant flag (483 false / 17 true) with little discriminating power for this query. Grounded but low leverage."
    }
  ],
  "analytical_usefulness": 0.62,
  "source_groundedness": 0.83,
  "rationale": "Most added columns provide genuine new axes (asset_category, form_factor, brand, travel_context, action_type, processing_lag) that are well-grounded in the ci and short_description text, directly supporting analysis of these expense records. A few columns are weak: source_id_present and is_miscellaneous_ci add little leverage, and department_group is largely redundant with an existing column while asserting per-row department values not visible in the sampled source text, raising a groundedness concern. Overall the set is useful and mostly grounded."
}
